description: Article chain detection. A boundary is the adjacent page pair (N, N+1); its endpoints are the last paragraph of page N and the first paragraph of page N+1 in derived reading order. A boundary is only scored when both pages carry a page kind whose policy sets chain_eligible; that mask is a qualification, not a term in the score. Each signal named by a weight_<signal> key returns a value in 0..1, and the boundary score is the weighted sum over the signals divided by the total positive weight, clamped to 0..1; a signal the geometry cannot supply contributes nothing. A negative weight is a soft prior that withdraws evidence rather than supplying any, so it stays out of the denominator, and the loader refuses a weight set in which a boundary carrying every signal at full strength could be pulled below link_min_score by the priors alone. That refusal is what keeps paragraph level evidence authoritative over the page level prior. terminal_punctuation lists the sentence enders, Latin and CJK, and terminal_closers the closing marks stripped from a tail before its ender is read, so a quoted sentence still reads as ended; both are written as JSON unicode escapes to keep this file ASCII. Retune the weights and thresholds here from the report produced by tools/chain_report.py, never in code.
